questions.problem: Given that $Q(2,4,1)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨-6,2,9⟩=5$, find the shortest distance from $P(6,-1,0)$ to $Π.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,4,1⟩-⟨6,-1,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,5,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-6,2,9⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-4)\cdot (-6)+5\cdot 2+1\cdot 9|}{\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{9}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|24+10+9|}{\sqrt{36+4+81}} \\  & =\frac{|43|}{\sqrt{121}} \\  & =\frac{43}{11}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(5,4,-4)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $6x-3y+6z=-18.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=1$ and $y=2$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}6x-3y+6z & =-18 \\ 6(1)-3(2)+6z & =-18 \\ 6z & =-18 \\ z & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(1,2,-3)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,2,-3⟩-⟨5,4,-4⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,-2,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨6,-3,6⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-4)\cdot 6+(-2)\cdot (-3)+1\cdot 6|}{\sqrt{{6}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{6}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-24+6+6|}{\sqrt{36+9+36}} \\  & =\frac{|\,-12\,|}{\sqrt{81}} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-11,-8,-4)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $14x+8y-8z=-6.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=-1$ and $y=-2$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}14x+8y-8z & =-6 \\ 14(-1)+8(-2)-8z & =-6 \\ -8z & =24 \\ z & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(-1,-2,-3)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨-1,-2,-3⟩-⟨-11,-8,-4⟩ \\  & =⟨10,6,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨14,8,-8⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|10\cdot 14+6\cdot 8+1\cdot (-8)|}{\sqrt{(14)^{2}+{8}^{2}+(-8)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|140+48-8|}{\sqrt{196+64+64}} \\  & =\frac{|\,180\,|}{\sqrt{324}} \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $Q(4,-2,8)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨-3,6,2⟩=-8$, find the shortest distance from $P(3,-4,2)$ to $Π.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨4,-2,8⟩-⟨3,-4,2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,2,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-3,6,2⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|1\cdot (-3)+2\cdot 6+6\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{6}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-3+12+12|}{\sqrt{9+36+4}} \\  & =\frac{|21|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{21}{7} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $Q(5,-1,9)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨3,-6,-2⟩=3$, find the shortest distance from $P(7,-2,8)$ to $Π.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨5,-1,9⟩-⟨7,-2,8⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨3,-6,-2⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-2)\cdot 3+1\cdot (-6)+1\cdot (-2)|}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-6)^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-6-6-2|}{\sqrt{9+36+4}} \\  & =\frac{|-14|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{14}{7} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
